headline: More IGF-1 in your blood
body: The growth plate only responds to what actually reaches it.
punch: Which is why delivery matters more than levels.

headline: The standard assumption
body: Raise systemic IGF-1, get more growth. It's the logic behind most of what gets sold in this space.
punch: Systemic and local are not the same variable.

headline: IGF-1 acts on cartilage
body: Growth plate chondrocytes produce IGF-1 themselves and respond to what's made in the tissue — autocrine and paracrine signalling, not just what arrives by blood.
punch: The tissue partly supplies its own signal.

headline: Which is why researchers
body: Cartilage-targeted IGF-1 delivery exists as an explicit strategy — engineering the molecule to concentrate where growth happens rather than everywhere at once.
punch: If systemic levels were sufficient, targeting would be pointless.

headline: And systemic IGF-1
body: Raise it everywhere and you also raise it in every other IGF-1-responsive tissue. The dose-limiting problem isn't the growth plate — it's everything else.
punch: You can't push a systemic signal hard enough to be locally optimal.

headline: Growth hormone
body: GH acts directly on human growth plate stem cells through JAK/STAT and local TGF-beta — independent of the liver IGF-1 pathway everyone measures.
punch: The GH axis has a local arm nobody tests for.

headline: So a blood test
body: Serum IGF-1 tells you about liver output. It does not tell you what concentration the resting zone is experiencing, and those can diverge.
punch: The number you can measure isn't the number that matters.

headline: The honest position
body: Local delivery is mechanistically compelling and actively researched. It is not an available intervention, and systemic manipulation is not a substitute for it.
punch: A better idea that doesn't exist yet is still not a thing you can use.

headline: It's never over
body: Real mechanisms, real citations, no protocols.
